title: Lift per-agent budget and timeout caps in athena.toml
summary: Edit nine values in athena.toml ([budget] and [job_plan]) per the owner's 4 Nov direction to lift caps. Values only; no keys added or removed, no schema change. Audience: the Athena owner and verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check the config parses and loads, not just that values were edited.
cargo test run by the verifier.
Config is parsed by existing schema tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: remove budget/time caps that are causing failed jobs, per the owner's direction; audience is the owner running Athena.
athena.toml is a governance file; it is listed as a deliverable and named in criteria.
Other keys (reader_timeout_s, check_timeout_s, planner/critic timeouts, priority_caps, forecast priors) stay unchanged as not listed.
I read athena.toml lines for the [budget] and [job_plan] keys; current values match the request's 'from' values.

acceptance_criteria.text: git diff shows athena.toml as the only changed file, with exactly these changes: reader_usd 0.50->2.00, producer_usd 3.00->10.00, verifier_usd 2.00->5.00, job_usd 12.00->40.00, producer_timeout_s 3000->5400, verifier_timeout_s 2400->3600 under [budget]; planner_usd 0.75->3.00, critic_usd 0.75->3.00, max_rounds 3->5 under [job_plan]; no other line differs.
Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-data`; it passes, so the new athena.toml parses against the config schema.

Run `cargo run --locked -- --help` or the repo's config-loading command if one exists (check README); the athena binary built from the repo loads the new athena.toml without error. If no read-only config-loading command exists, the cargo test criterion stands as evidence.
crates/athena-data/src/config.rs is unchanged and no key in athena.toml was added or removed (git diff shows only value substitutions).

out_of_scope: Changing keys not listed (reader_timeout_s, check_timeout_s, planner_timeout_s, critic_timeout_s)
departures: Trivial value-only edit to one file, so cheaper, faster and likelier to pass than the reference.
